business_type: mature compounder (subscription software under a disruption narrative)
moat_source: professional-workflow switching costs, file-format/ecosystem standards (PSD, PDF), and enterprise contract embedding; evidence: +12.7% revenue growth with raised guidance DURING peak disruption fear - customers are not leaving while the market prices as if they already have

returns.assumption_note: Convergence to scenario IV by year 5, ~60% of the gap closed by year 3. All scenario cash flows are SBC-adjusted (full 1.94B annual haircut) and equity values net of the 1.02B net debt - the audit fixes applied. Buyback accretion at a 13% FCF yield is NOT modeled and would add materially to base/bull outcomes.

sensitivity_key_driver: terminal multiple (what a slower-growth but cash-gushing Adobe is worth in 2031)
primary_model_risk: Disruption slope: the bear case assumes generative AI (Claude Design, Midjourney, Sora, Canva) erodes ARR growth to zero by 2028 and compresses FCF ~35% by 2030. That is a genuine possibility, not a strawman - the entire margin of safety depends on the erosion being slower or shallower than the market's already-priced assumption. The reported evidence to date (beats, raised guidance, ARR +10.2%) sides with the base case; narratives can outrun evidence for years.
expectations_gap_key_variable: ARR trajectory: at $221.54 (~9x forward earnings, ~10x FCF) the price implies revenue and cash flow DECLINE beginning within two years; reported ARR is growing 10.2% with guidance just raised - the market and the filings currently describe two different companies, and our base case simply believes the filings with a decelerating haircut
top_5_bull_arguments: First 'market too pessimistic' verdict in 23 analyses: a 13.15% FCF yield on a wide-moat franchise that just RAISED guidance
Every reported number contradicts the decline narrative: revenue +12.7% (beat), EPS beat, ARR +10.2%, FY guide raised ~600M
At ~10x FCF, buybacks retire ~10% of shares annually - the do-nothing scenario compounds per-share value double-digits
Third-party fair values (314-328) and consensus targets (272) all sit far above the price - even skeptics cannot model it this low
Enterprise creative/document workflows are contractual and compliance-embedded; disruption of professional seats moves slower than prosumer headlines
top_5_bear_arguments: Technological risk is High and real: generative tools attack the low end first, then move up - the classic disruption path, and Claude Design/Canva are moving fast
ARR deceleration (10.2% and drifting down) is the crack the bears are watching; pricing power erosion shows up there first
CEO transition during a narrative crisis raises execution risk
SBC data conflict: if the 1.94B figure is genuinely quarterly (~7.8B/yr), SBC-adjusted FCF collapses to ~4B and the value case fails - resolution against the 10-K is mandatory before deployment
Cheap software with a secular question is exactly how Citrix/Teradata traded on the way down - value_trap Medium, not Low
thesis_breakers: Ending ARR growth below 7% y/y (erosion accelerating)
First y/y decline in Creative Cloud net new ARR
FY2026 revenue guidance cut (reversing the raise)
SBC verified above $4B/yr (per-share economics materially worse than modeled)
Enterprise seat churn disclosures or a flagship enterprise loss to a generative-AI competitor
position_size_recommendation: 3-4% starter with room to add - the first name analyzed that offers a positive margin of safety WITH positive expected returns across base and bull; size reflects the genuinely live disruption tail (bear 30%)
notes_on_nulls: ROIC/ROE/ROA null: not captured as sourced ratios. Audit fixes from the 2026-07-08 methodology review are applied here: SBC fully deducted (1.94B, conflict-flagged), net debt (1.02B, sourced) netted from equity value, and the returns note quantifies what buybacks would add. Revenue/EPS/guidance/FCF-yield/balance-sheet inputs are all reported or aggregator-sourced - confidence_level medium pending SBC verification against the 10-K.
historical_context: Directional context only - low confidence. Verified datapoints: stock down 30-37% in 2026 across coverage, forward P/E ~9 with PEG 0.6 (Yahoo/247wallst), FCF yield 13.15% vs its own 12-month average of 8.30% (financecharts - a sourced historical comparison, rare in this run), 52-week decline ~41%. The FCF-yield-vs-own-average gap is the single most concrete historical-valuation datapoint captured in any of the 23 analyses.
